transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Sara Lowe (Emberline - Head of ML), David Kim (Emberline - Platform), Priya Nair (Emberline - CTO), Tom Carr (Emberline - SRE)

Summary:
Quick sprint-style readout of the week's benchmark runs comparing Redwood pilot cluster to their current baseline (IncumbentAI). Focus on tail latency regressions seen under 95/99, throughput at 1k qps and realistic burst patterns, and routing/fallback behavior when dedicated capacity is exhausted. Agreed next steps for microbench on KV/prefix cache and proposed 2-week dedicated slot trial.

Topics covered:
- Latency vs baseline (95/99)
- Throughput and burst handling
- KV cache/prefix caching and caching mis-hits
- Routing policy: latency-first vs cost-first
- Dedicated slot request and isolation concerns
- Security/VPC peering quick check

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday morning, we know you had a busy weekend with the lab runs, so appreciate the time. I think we have about 50 minutes scheduled, we'll run through the numbers Raj put in the spreadsheet and then talk action items.
[00:18] Sara (Emberline): Thanks Maya, yeah we had the team running the full traffic pattern overnight. We saw some, uh, interesting 95th/99th spikes around the tail - looked higher than the baseline for a couple of model sizes.
[00:30] Raj (SE): Yeah, on the 13B quantized run we saw steady p50 at like 42ms but p95 jumped to 220ms on bursts. baseline shows p95 at ~160ms so there is a delta. we suspect cache warm-up + routing fallback interplay.
[00:50] David (Platform): Quick clarification - the baseline was the IncumbentAI managed endpoint, correct? same request shapes?
[00:57] Sara: correct, we replayed a 24 hour production trace, kept prompt lengths and batching consistent, used their recommended batching heuristics.
[01:10] Raj: Right, the difference though is how Redwood is handling prefix/KV caching. Our default was enabled but we noticed cache eviction on longer sessions. I want to call out there may be a misconfiguration in their replay harness that wasn't pinning session keys, so some cache warm-ups were lost.
[01:30] Tom (SRE): Yeah we might have not persisted the session id properly in the trace, that could explain the miss pattern. we'll check.
[01:40] Maya: Ok good, that's a cheap win if it's just replay harness. But there were also cases where the routing engine moved requests to a fallback model variant when the dedicated pool hit its soft limit. That fallback path introduced additional latencies.
[01:58] Priya (CTO): Can you unpack the fallback path? Is that because of instance spin-up or is it a cross-region hop?
[02:05] Raj: So two things - one, we've got a policy that will route to a lower-cost compatible variant to maintain availability under load. two, if the dedicated pool is saturated we route to shared capacity in a different availability zone which does add network hop and cold KV-cache if not primed.
[02:25] Sara: That explains the sudden 300ms+ tails we saw. The baseline had a larger reserved capacity so didn't fall back.
[02:35] Raj: Exactly. For the immediate sprint we recommend: 1) run a prefix-cache-only microbench to verify warm-up patterns; 2) tweak the soft limit to allow burst headroom for your traffic shape; 3) capture full trace including session id so we can replay exactly.
[02:56] Maya: I'm going to share an updated routing config suggestion in the spreadsheet. Also note that quantization profile differences affect decode speed, so the 4-bit profile we used might have slightly different kernel runtime characteristics vs the baseline's 8-bit mixed profile.
[03:15] David: The baseline is indeed using 8-bit mixed for 13B - might be why p50 is a bit better for them in steady state. but the vendor numbers from their whitepaper don't match our in-practice numbers.
[03:28] Raj: There's also the batch assembly behavior — IncumbentAI aggregates at 8-12 tokens and we saw Redwood's default batching target at 16 tokens in the runner when burst traffic hits. That can shift latency distribution.
[03:45] Speaker 3: (mumbled) ... batching target, yeah there's an interplay with request size...
[03:52] Raj: Back to the numbers on the sheet: the worst p99 was 810ms for one outlier run when the fallback kicked in and we also had a cache miss storm due to session id. Without fallback the p99 drops to ~360ms which is closer to expectations.
[04:12] Sara: ok so we need two things: eliminate harness id issue, and then re-run with the routing soft limit higher?
[04:20] Maya: Yes. We also proposed a short dedicated slot for two weeks so you have reserved headroom while we fine tune routing and cache. That will remove the fallback-to-shared path entirely for the trial.
[04:33] Priya: Cost question — what's the delta for the 2-week dedicated slot vs what we're paying now? We need unit-cost comparisons because procurement will balk if cost is higher without clear latency improvements.
[04:44] Maya: We'll put a simple delta column in the spreadsheet. High-level: dedicated increases monthly committed cost but reduces per-token variability and fallback-induced tail latency, which tends to lower overall unit cost at scale due to fewer retries and faster completion. We'll compute both per-request token cost and projected 95th-tail penalty.
[05:03] Lena (CSM): I'll coordinate with your finance contact as well to get a rough TCO comparison.
[05:10] Tom: Quick security/VPC check — we did an initial peering test and there were three blocked ports. we fixed two but one still needs a change from your side.
[05:20] Maya: Which one?
[05:22] Tom: Outbound 9301 from the bastion to the Redwood egress IP isn't allowed. We'll send the firewall rule snippet.
[05:30] Maya: We'll get infra to open that. send to maya@redwood and cc raj.
[05:35] David: On the test design, can we keep the same seed traffic but add a synthetic spike at minute 30 to stress the fallback logic?
[05:44] Raj: Yes we actually added that as test A3, it's in the sheet called "burst-30m-synth". that run shows the worst-case behavior.
[05:52] Sara: So timeline: you run the microbench and ignite a replay with session id fixed, we re-run the full 24-hour trace with higher soft limit, and if that looks good we'll start the 2-week dedicated slot.
[06:05] Maya: Correct. Does Emberline want the dedicated slot to be isolated to region west-2?
[06:12] Priya: West-2 yes, because of data residency for some logs. Also we'd like audit logs forwarded to our KMS-enabled bucket.
[06:20] Raj: We can enable KMS integration for the trial; logs can be forwarded, though for compliance we may have to provide a short runbook for audit.
[06:28] Sara: We'll need SOC2 attestations and how long logs are retained.
[06:32] Maya: We'll share the security pack; Lena will attach SOC2 and the retention options.
[06:38] Tom: Also, do you support customer-managed HSM? for key separation?
[06:42] Raj: Yes, for Private deployments we support HSM/KMS and in some cases bring-your-own-hsm with an HSM connector. For hosted pilot we can enable cross-account KMS policies. I'll put exact steps in the security note.
[06:55] Maya: Cool. Any other blockers from the team?
[07:00] Sara: One more: can we get per-model kernel selection logs to understand which kernels fired on the 13B runs? The baseline vendor claims a custom kernel.
[07:09] Raj: We can export kernel traces, yes — they'll be in the perf artifact zip. note that naming in the trace might be slightly different, sometimes shows like "matmul_opt_v2" vs their "matmulX" naming, so mapping required.
[07:26] David: Also please include tokenization breakdown per request, some of our prompts have long instruction tokens which inflate time.
[07:33] Raj: Will do.
[07:35] Speaker 2: (briefly) ...
[07:40] Maya: Ok, to recap: action items as we discussed - Maya share updated spreadsheet and routing suggestion; Raj run prefix-cache microbench + kernel traces; Tom finalize firewall rule and confirm peering; Sara confirm success criteria and signoff window; Lena share SOC2 + security pack. We aim to have re-run results by Monday (2026-09-20) and dedicated slot sign-off by 2026-09-22.
[08:05] Priya: That timeline works for us, assuming the microbench shows the p95 improvement.
[08:12] Maya: One more note — we noticed IncumbentAI was using slightly larger instance types for the same model which reduced tokenization jitter. We can recommend a temporary bump in vCPU for the pilot to match that, if you want.
[08:24] Sara: That could be useful for apples-to-apples. please include estimated cost delta.
[08:31] Raj: I'll add a small section in the spreadsheet with an instance size sensitivity table.
[08:36] Tom: Also, for the dedicated slot trial we want a kill-switch automation if error rate creeps above 2% for more than 5 minutes. can you support that?
[08:46] Maya: Yes we have an automated rollback/runbook we can wire into your alerting. We'll provide an initial policy template.
[08:52] Lena: I'll take the lead on operational runbooks and handoff.
[08:55] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. we'll circulate the notes and next steps.
[09:00] End meeting.
